question: Leap Day, February \(29,\) \(2004,\) occurred on a Sunday. On what day of the week will Leap Day, February \(29,\) \(2020,\) occur?
solution:
Weekdays repeat every \(7\) days, so complete weeks do not change the weekday.

The successive Leap Days here occur in \(2004,2008,2012,2016,2020\). Between each pair of successive Leap Days there are four years of \(365\) days plus one extra February day, giving
\[
4\cdot365+1=1461\text{ days}.
\]
There are four such intervals from \(2004\) to \(2020\), so the elapsed time is
\[
4\cdot1461=5844=7\cdot834+6\text{ days}.
\]
The weekday therefore advances \(6\) days. Six days after Sunday is \(\boxed{\text{Saturday}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).

(Commutative property of multiplication.) 3 × 5 × 2 can be found by 3 × 5 = 15, then 15 × 2 = 30, or by 5 × 2 = 10, then 3 × 10 = 30. (Associative property of multiplication.) Knowing that 8 × 5 = 40 and 8 × 2 = 16, one can find 8 × 7 as 8 × (5 + 2) = (8 × 5) + (8 × 2) = 40 + 16 = 56. (Distributive property.) *Students need not use formal terms for these properties.

edges.reason: Exact table-division practice prepares the contrast with leftovers. Physical equal grouping directly establishes quotient, remainder and the smaller-than-divisor condition without a fact-based quotient algorithm.
The remainder is what is left after equal sharing, and the quotient is the number of equal groups. Interpreting either one presupposes division as equal sharing or grouping.
